children: HDFC Bank shares surged over 3 per cent on Tuesday after the bank moved ahead with its CEO succession process, submitting the names of two candidates to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for approval.

The stock traded at ₹726.55 on the NSE at 10.02 am, soaring to an intraday high of ₹730.75 from the previous close of ₹708.25. The stock’s movement came after HDFC Bank shortlisted two candidates whose names will be submitted to the RBI for approval to occupy the top position at the bank for three years.

The board of HDFC Bank may have shortlisted its Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha and K Balasubramanian, Citi’s Chief Country Officer for India, for getting RBI approval to appoint one of them as the bank’s chief, a report said.
The central bank usually requires private sector banks to propose two names who fit the bill in terms of its “fit and proper” criteria for the top position.
Earlier, on Saturday, HDFC Bank had shortlisted “two candidates” whose names will be submitted to the RBI so that it can approve one to occupy the top position at the bank for three years.
The board also took other important decisions, including the creation of an additional position of Whole-Time Director (WTD) to have a larger pipeline for succession planning.
The board also appointed Tata as a WTD, designated as Executive Director (ED), and re-appointed V Srinivasa Rangan as a WTD, designated as ED.
At the time of writing, the traded volume stood at 233.86 lakh shares, while the traded value was ₹1,697.92 crore. The total market capitalisation stood at ₹11.19 lakh crore.
The stock’s lower band and upper band have been fixed at ₹637.35 and ₹779.05, respectively, on the NSE. The adjusted P/E ratio stood at 13.62.

title: HDFC Bank shares surge over 3% as CEO succession process moves ahead
